parameters.query:
WITH cfg AS (
  SELECT body, sha256 FROM triage.config WHERE name = 'config.yaml'
),
rules AS (
  SELECT sha256 FROM triage.config WHERE name = 'rules.js'
),
-- The ruleset names the rules and config this run triages with. Verdicts are
-- kept per ruleset, so a changed rules.js or config.yaml re-triages open PRs.
active AS (
  SELECT 'r' || left(rules.sha256, 12) || '.c' || left(cfg.sha256, 12) AS ruleset FROM cfg, rules
),
run AS (
  INSERT INTO triage.runs (started, ruleset) VALUES (now(), (SELECT ruleset FROM active)) RETURNING id, ruleset
),
-- Same pattern as reposFromConfigLine() in rules.js; the Triage node checks they agree.
repos AS (
  SELECT btrim(r, ' "''') AS repo
  FROM cfg, regexp_split_to_table((regexp_match(E'\n' || cfg.body, '\nrepos:\s*\[([^\]\n]*)\]'))[1], ',') AS r
),
-- Only an ETag stored under this ruleset: a 304 from an older one would skip the re-triage.
last AS (
  SELECT list_etags FROM triage.runs
  WHERE finished IS NOT NULL AND ruleset = (SELECT ruleset FROM active)
  ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  run.id AS run_id,
  run.ruleset,
  repos.repo,
  (SELECT list_etags ->> repos.repo FROM last) AS list_etag,
  cfg.body AS config_body,
  cfg.sha256 AS config_sha,
  (SELECT coalesce(json_agg(pattern ORDER BY pattern), '[]'::json) FROM triage.redaction_patterns) AS patterns,
  -- A head SHA is done once it has a verdict under this ruleset, or a finalised one under any.
  (SELECT coalesce(json_agg(DISTINCT repo || '#' || pr || '@' || head_sha), '[]'::json)
     FROM triage.verdicts
     WHERE created > now() - interval '90 days'
       AND (ruleset = run.ruleset OR finalised_at IS NOT NULL)) AS seen,
  -- The latest verdict per head SHA, with each check's result, so the Triage node
  -- can carry an unchanged result forward. A carried row's checks come from the
  -- full row it names, and id is that full row.
  (SELECT coalesce(json_object_agg(k, p), '{}'::json) FROM (
     SELECT DISTINCT ON (v.repo, v.pr, v.head_sha)
       v.repo || '#' || v.pr || '@' || v.head_sha AS k,
       json_build_object(
         'id', coalesce(v.carried_from, v.id),
         'verdict', v.verdict,
         'results', (SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('id', c ->> 'id', 'result', c ->> 'result') ORDER BY n)
                       FROM jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(v.checks, src.checks)) WITH ORDINALITY AS e (c, n))) AS p
     FROM triage.verdicts v
     LEFT JOIN triage.verdicts src ON src.id = v.carried_from
     WHERE v.created > now() - interval '90 days'
     ORDER BY v.repo, v.pr, v.head_sha, v.id DESC) latest) AS previous,
  -- For the digest: the latest verdict each head SHA has under this ruleset, or a
  -- finalised one under any.
  (SELECT coalesce(json_object_agg(k, c), '{}'::json) FROM (
     SELECT DISTINCT ON (repo, pr, head_sha)
       repo || '#' || pr || '@' || head_sha AS k,
       json_build_object('verdict', verdict, 'reasons', reasons, 'finalised', finalised_at IS NOT NULL) AS c
     FROM triage.verdicts
     WHERE created > now() - interval '90 days'
       AND (ruleset = run.ruleset OR finalised_at IS NOT NULL)
     ORDER BY repo, pr, head_sha, id DESC) cur) AS current_verdicts,
  -- The digest issue and the sha256 of the body last read back from it.
  d.issue_number AS digest_issue,
  d.body_sha256 AS digest_sha
FROM run
LEFT JOIN cfg ON true
LEFT JOIN repos ON true
LEFT JOIN triage.digest d ON d.repo = repos.repo;

nodes.name: Open PRs
nodes.notes: For the digest: the open PRs as they are now. Unlike List PRs, no ETag, so a 304 never hides them.

nodes.name: Who am I
nodes.notes: For the digest: the token's own login. The digest issue is looked up among issues this login opened, never a hardcoded name.

nodes.name: Digest issues
nodes.notes: For the digest: issues the token opened, any state. Triage picks the stored one, or the one with the marker.

nodes.name: One item per PR
nodes.notes: A 304 or an empty list gives no items; alwaysOutputData then passes one empty placeholder, so Triage still runs.

nodes.name: Cluster version
nodes.notes: Runs the unsaved sub-workflow that reads the service-account token, so the token never enters this workflow's saved run data.

parameters.query:
-- All of the run's verdicts in one statement, so the chain goes on when there
-- are none. A carried row (checks null, carried_from set) records that this
-- ruleset gave the same verdict and check results as the full row it names.
-- finalise is set only for a human verdict whose R9 passed.
WITH v AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS x (
    run_id bigint, repo text, pr integer, head_sha text, verdict text, reasons jsonb,
    checks jsonb, ruleset text, carried_from bigint, finalise boolean)
),
ins AS (
  INSERT INTO triage.verdicts (run_id, repo, pr, head_sha, verdict, reasons, checks, ruleset, carried_from, finalised_at)
  SELECT run_id, repo, pr, head_sha, verdict, reasons, NULLIF(checks, 'null'::jsonb), ruleset, NULLIF(carried_from, 0),
         CASE WHEN finalise THEN now() END
  FROM v
  ON CONFLICT (repo, pr, head_sha, ruleset) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT count(*) AS inserted FROM ins;

UPDATE triage.runs
SET finished = now(),
    pr_count = (SELECT count(*) FROM triage.verdicts WHERE run_id = $1),
    negative_control = $2,
    ok = $3,
    list_etags = $4::jsonb,
    -- write_mode off: no write node runs. digest: Record digest fills it in.
    digest = CASE WHEN $5::text = 'digest' THEN NULL ELSE 'off' END
WHERE id = $1;

nodes.name: Write gate
nodes.notes: Every GitHub write sits after the true output (write_mode digest). sync-code-nodes.js refuses any that does not, and any write but the two digest requests.

nodes.name: Create digest issue
nodes.notes: Only when no issue of ours has the marker. Title and body only.

nodes.name: Edit digest issue
nodes.notes: The body only: never title, state, labels or assignees.

nodes.name: Read back digest issue
nodes.notes: A failed write reads rate_limit instead, which never matches, so Record digest records failed.

parameters.query:
-- One row per repo. A skip brings its own outcome. After a write, the outcome is
-- published only if the readback holds the body that was sent, marker first
-- (digestReadback in rules.js), else failed. body_sha256 is stored only when
-- published, so the next run retries a failed write.
WITH input AS (
  SELECT $1::bigint AS run_id, $2::text AS repo, NULLIF($3::integer, 0) AS issue_number,
    CASE
      WHEN $4::text <> '' THEN $4::text
      WHEN starts_with($5::text, '<!-- pr-triage-digest:v1 -->')
           AND encode(sha256(convert_to($5::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') = $6::text THEN 'published'
      ELSE 'failed'
    END AS status,
    $6::text AS body_sha256
),
saved AS (
  INSERT INTO triage.digest AS d (repo, issue_number, body_sha256, status, published_at, checked)
  SELECT repo, issue_number,
         CASE WHEN status = 'published' THEN body_sha256 END,
         status,
         CASE WHEN status = 'published' THEN now() END,
         now()
  FROM input
  ON CONFLICT (repo) DO UPDATE SET
    issue_number = coalesce(excluded.issue_number, d.issue_number),
    body_sha256 = CASE WHEN excluded.status = 'published' THEN excluded.body_sha256 ELSE d.body_sha256 END,
    status = excluded.status,
    published_at = coalesce(excluded.published_at, d.published_at),
    checked = excluded.checked
  RETURNING status
)
UPDATE triage.runs AS r
SET digest = concat_ws(',', r.digest, s.status),
    ok = coalesce(r.ok, false) AND s.status NOT IN ('failed', 'redaction-hit')
FROM saved s
WHERE r.id = (SELECT run_id FROM input)
RETURNING r.id, r.digest, r.ok;
